I queued one Short for Hopeverse Media (yt-hopeverse), on the planned Lula topic. Nothing is published until you review it.

**Title:** "80 Years Old, 4th Term: Lula Wins Brazil #Shorts"
**Queued as:** `yt-hopeverse-15.json`

**What I decided and why**
- **Topic:** The Lula story hadn't been drafted yet, and it's from the last 48 hours. Mr. Focus confirmed it from NPR and CNBC, with Fox relaying AP. Both quote Brazil's electoral court: Lula took about 51.8% to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2% in the 25 October runoff.
- **Change from the plan:** The planned framing was wrong in one way. Lula came second in the first round. NPR and CNBC report that no first-round runner-up had won a runoff since 1989, so that comeback became the hook.
- **India angle:** India chairs BRICS in 2026. It's a strong, balanced hook for Indian viewers and could become a repeatable "world news, India angle" series.
- **Search problems:** Mr. Focus ran out of search quota, so today's list of 5 topics came back empty. He offered science and trivia ideas instead. I turned those down because you ruled out trivia on 26 October.
- **Late fix:** Mr. Pen wrote the script before the result was confirmed, so it named no winner. After the fact-check confirmed the result, I rewrote it myself rather than paying for a second Mr. Pen call.
- **Kept neutral:** No politician faces or voices, and no mention of Bolsonaro reportedly refusing to concede or asking for the result to be annulled.

**Before publishing, please check:*

I queued one Short for Sankalp, but it's a recap of a story from 25 July, not news from the last 48 hours. Mr. Focus ran out of searches, couldn't build today's top-5 list, and couldn't confirm the planned topic. Please review it before it goes out at 21:00 IST.

**Title:** 25 July 2026: Pradhan Resigns, Protests End #Shorts

**Why the planned topic didn't work**
- **The minister's resignation:** Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on 25 July 2026, about 93 days ago, so it's too old to count as new.
- **Abhijeet Dipke's detention:** the reports Mr. Focus found were from 10 and 16 October. The fact-check couldn't confirm either one, so I left them out.
- **New policy this week:** none found.
- **Repeat risk:** Sankalp already covered the paper-leak law ("10 Years Jail…"), so I kept this from repeating it.
- **Date mismatch:** Mr. Focus thought today was around 26 October, but the plan says Thursday 29 October. The script gives exact dates and never says "today" or "this week".

**What the fact-check changed**
Mr. Pen's first draft failed the fact-check. Three claims couldn't be confirmed, so I cut them:
- the "two million candidates re-test" figure;
- the claim that Modi promised fast-track courts and a new law;
- the 10 October detention, and the claim that the movement now targets the Chief Election Commissioner.

I also changed the opinion lines Mr. Focus said were unfair. "Accountability reached the top" became "stepped down under pressure", and I dropped "the paper-leak demand is

I queued one Short for yt-hopeverse, on the planned France protests topic. It isn't published yet. A second fact-check couldn't re-confirm four facts against a news wire (AP or Reuters), so the package is marked HOLD until you spot-check them against AP.

**Title:** 289 Protests Began at One School #Shorts

**Why this topic:**
- **Still new and current:** it isn't in the outbox, and the protests were on 24 Oct, inside the 48-hour window.
- **Mostly accurate:** Mr. Focus's research backed most of the brief with AP, Reuters/CBC and France 24.
- **No India story was possible:** the run also asked for a Short for Indian viewers. Mr. Focus's search quota ran out before he could source today's topics. His backup ideas were animal and science trivia, which your 26 Oct rule bans.
- **Exactly one Short per run:** so I made the verified planned topic. It is for the international audience, not India. If today's 4 India slots are short by one, a later run should fill it.

**Two changes from the brief to keep it accurate:**
- **Arrests:** the brief's "more than 1,300" isn't an official figure. The Short now says the interior minister reported nearly 1,000 and France 24 later reported 1,314, and adds "arrests are not convictions."
- **Election date:** "May 2027" became "spring 2027", because the vote is in two rounds, April and May.

It stays neutral, attributes every disputed number to whoever gave it, and shows no clashes, injuries or party emblems.

**What was queued:** the final script

I couldn't find any news story from the last 48 hours: Mr. Focus's search quota ran out, so the planned India–world slot (US trade or tariffs, or a foreign policy move) could not be dated or confirmed by two sources. Instead I queued a Sawaal explainer on electoral bonds that doesn't depend on today's news.

**Decision and why**
- **Planned topic:** it had no story attached and couldn't be checked, so I didn't make up news to fill it. The plan says every run queues one Short, so I picked a topic whose facts are settled.
- **Electoral bonds:** it fits Sawaal's niche (questions the government must answer), people search for it, and it's new for this channel. Sawaal's two earlier Shorts were the voter-roll petition and the BRICS forum.
- **Facts used:** only ones confirmed by at least two sources in the 2024 Supreme Court case:
  - the unanimous five-judge ruling on 15 Feb 2024;
  - the main ground, voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a);
  - the three laws whose amendments were struck down;
  - the court refusing SBI's request for time until 30 June.
- **Fact-check fixes:**
  - "Six years" became "about six years."
  - The government's argument now says the court rejected it.
  - The "wilful disobedience" quote is now paraphrased.
  - One misleading line ("data the court ordered in a day") now says the court asked for the data "within weeks."
- **Left out:** rupee totals, party-wise shares and anything suggesting corruption, because none of it could be confirmed.

I queued one Short for Instinct, the planned tardigrade topic in French. It's in the queue as `yt-instinct-3.json` and nothing is published until you review and upload it.

**Title:** « 3 tardigrades ont survécu aux UV en orbite #Shorts »

**Why this topic:** Instinct hadn't covered it yet. Its only earlier Shorts were the octopus and the dolphin, and I checked the outbox, so it isn't a repeat. It's a well-documented science story rather than news, which suits the channel. The research turned up a hook that corrects the usual myth: dried tardigrades survived the vacuum of space, but the sun's UV killed most of them. The title starts with a number, like the channel's earlier Shorts. It's a narrator-only Short in French, with no recurring characters, made from stock footage and labelled AI images.

**Fact-check changes:**
- **Opening line:** "but not the sun" was wrong, because 3 tardigrades did survive full UV. It now says the UV "almost got the better of them".
- **Species:** the script now says there were two species, not one.
- **"Mystery" line:** I cut "researchers call it a mystery" and replaced it with "the question remains open". The first research pass quoted the authors using that word, but the fact-check couldn't confirm it.
- **Myths left out:** the Short never calls tardigrades immortal, and doesn't say they "live in space" or that 68% survived.
- **Description:** I fixed two lines in the description myself. "Only three of them survived" became "only three *Milnesi

I queued one Sankalp Short for 9 PM IST. Search was down, so it's an evergreen explainer on the Women's Reservation Act, not a story from the last 48 hours.

**Title:** 454 बनाम 2: महिला आरक्षण कब लागू? #Shorts (English master: "454 to 2: Women's Quota Explained #Shorts")

**Why I didn't use the planned topic:** Sankalp has already drafted "Pradhan Resigns, Protests End" and "India's Paper Leak Law Explained". The planned topic (the minister's exit and the paper-leak response) mostly repeats those. Mr. Focus also couldn't open the CNN article to see if it reports any new step since July. The daily search for today's top stories then failed because the search limit was used up.

**Why this topic:** It's a settled story with clear numbers, a strong hook ("the law is passed, so why no seats yet?") and an obvious national-pride angle. It puts the critics' complaint about the wait fairly, then makes the case for doing the census first. The "what next" view on how reserved seats will rotate is marked as opinion. It doesn't repeat anything in the outbox.

**Fact-check:** Search was working again for the fact-check, and seven of eight claims were confirmed, mostly by explainer sites rather than official records. The eighth needed a wording fix. I changed four things before queueing:
- Only one source gave the 2023 Rajya Sabha count of 214–0, so the script says "no votes against" instead.
- "Lasts 15 years" now says the 15 years run from when the quota starts.
- The census date of 1 M
